advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the disposition-attestation read is protected by (or ordered after) the store-freshness guard so a stale store cannot mint/deny a disposition verdict.
evidence: close_precheck.py:659-661: `disposition = _administrative_disposition(...)` returns `disposition, "disposition"` before the freshness guard

close_precheck.py:672-673: `# Gate is ON and unforced: refuse a stale store BEFORE the billable verifier (bug b928).` `freshness.assert_gate_store_fresh(...)` now runs only AFTER the disposition return
Original code ran assert_gate_store_fresh immediately after the skip check, before close_class_refusal and any disposition read (removed block at close_precheck old lines 630-636)
advisory.finding: Both disposition-attestation paths now read the tracker for replacement links / reasons BEFORE the store-freshness guard, whereas the completion path keeps that guard first. In close_precheck the disposition check (_administrative_disposition) runs at line 659-661, returning before assert_gate_store_fresh at line 673; in gates the _disposition_close_exempt call (line 227) runs before store_freshness (line 248). A stale ticket store can therefore mint or deny a disposition attestation with no freshness check.
scenarios: A disposition close decided against a tracker store that is not current: a replacement link or reason read from a stale store yields a false disposition verdict (either wrongly granting the exemption or wrongly withholding it) with no staleness refusal.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a non-force administrative disposition close (e.g. `--class=superseded` / `--class=obsolete --reason=...`) succeeds even when the completion gate store is stale, pinning the reordered freshness-vs-disposition precedence.
evidence: Old order (removed): the skip/`freshness.assert_gate_store_fresh("the completion close gate", ...)` block ran BEFORE `disposition = _administrative_disposition(...)`.

New order (added at close_precheck.py:663-673): `# Administrative dispositions are checked first ...` then `skip = _gate_skip_expectation(...)` / `freshness.assert_gate_store_fresh(...)` now sit AFTER `if disposition is not _NO_DISPOSITION: return disposition, "disposition"` (line 660-661).

ABSENCE: `search_files` for `assert_gate_store_fresh` and `stale` under tests/ returns no test exercising a disposition close against a stale gate store; the new interface tests (test_open_task_obsolete_close_bypasses_plan_review_close_gate) never advance HEAD/stale the store.
advisory.finding: The close_precheck reorder moves `freshness.assert_gate_store_fresh` to AFTER the administrative-disposition short-circuit for non-force closes, newly allowing a disposition close (e.g. `--class=superseded`, `--class=obsolete --reason=...`) to succeed against a STALE completion-gate store — a case that was previously refused (the b928 freshness guard ran unconditionally before the disposition check). No test asserts this newly-permitted outcome.
scenarios: A non-force administrative close (superseded/duplicate/obsolete/wontfix) attempted while the completion gate store is stale.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add or extend an end-to-end close test for `--class=wontfix --reason=...` asserting the close succeeds and a reason-backed disposition attestation is signed.
evidence: Interface test test_open_task_obsolete_close_bypasses_plan_review_close_gate uses close_class="obsolete" only; no wontfix end-to-end close asserting `close_class`=="wontfix" plus a verified completion-verifier/disposition signature.

close_disposition.verdict treats obsolete and wontfix identically via REASON_REQUIRED_CLASSES (close_disposition.py:195-202), so the gate-level parametrization gives partial confidence, but the CLI close-and-sign path is not exercised for wontfix.
advisory.finding: `wontfix` is exercised only at the gate-function level (parametrized in test_reason_required_classes_exempt_only_with_the_signed_reason); the full CLI close path that mints the reason-backed disposition attestation is proven end-to-end only for obsolete (interface) and superseded/duplicate (unit _close), leaving the wontfix end-to-end close-and-sign path unasserted.
scenarios: A non-force `--class=wontfix --reason=...` close on a plan-review-gated ticket.

dropped.finding: _disposition_close_exempt dropped its ticket_type parameter and now delegates to close_disposition.verdict/find_replacement, which the code documents (close_disposition.py:154-156) as 'strictly MORE permissive for non-bug tickets than close_precheck._has_live_replacement_link's extra ADMINISTRATIVE_CLASSES narrowing'.
